note: Baltic Sea undersea cable/pipeline damage incidents 2022-2026. Different incident type from ship attacks: intent is contested per case. IMO numbers not published in the source. Seed list, not exhaustive.

items.description: Nord Stream 1 and 2 pipelines ruptured (three of four lines). Sweden found explosive traces. Sweden and Denmark closed investigations in 2024 with no suspects named; no claim of responsibility.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)

items.locationText: Gulf of Finland / Baltic Sea (exact position not given)
items.description: Balticconnector gas pipeline (Finland-Estonia) and telecom cables severed. Finnish investigators found the ship dragged its anchor. Captain charged with criminal damage in Hong Kong.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)

items.description: Lithuania-Gotland (Telia) and Helsinki-Rostock (Cinia) telecom cables broke. Chinese bulk carrier from Ust-Luga; Reuters analysis of MarineTraffic data placed it at both breaches. Swedish inquiry (Apr 2025) found no conclusive evidence of deliberate anchor dragging.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)

items.description: Estlink 2 power cable and four telecom lines damaged. Cook Islands-flagged tanker described as shadow fleet. Seized 26 Dec 2024. Oct 2025 Finnish court dismissed case against captain and crew: intent not proven.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)

items.description: Latvia-Gotland fibre cable damaged; Cinia C-Lion1 also damaged around the same time (no vessel linked). Sweden first suspected gross sabotage; operator said anchor snagged in high winds. Swedish prosecutor ruled breach accidental and released the Maltese-flagged bulk carrier.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)

items.description: Helsinki-Estonia telecom cable and a second Arelion Finland-Estonia cable damaged; Estonia-Sweden cable failed 30 Dec. Cargo vessel from Russia to Israel reportedly dragging anchor; Finnish police seized it, two crew arrested. Investigation ongoing.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)

items.description: Arelion telecom cable damaged. Latvian police boarded a ship at Liepaja; on 5 Jan said no evidence linking the ship to the damage. Investigation continuing.
items.goldRef: Baird Maritime factbox (secondary source; verify against national investigation bodies before treating as gold)
